description: An atom is the smallest unit of matter, consisting primarily of electrons, protons, and neutrons. Understanding atomic structure and isotopes is crucial for applications in medicine, scientific research, and energy generation.

sections.title: Fundamental Particles of an Atom
sections.description: An atom consists mainly of three subatomic particles that determine its mass and electrical charge.

key_concepts.explanation: A negatively charged particle that revolves around the nucleus of the atom in fixed, discrete orbits.
A positively charged particle located inside the dense central nucleus of the atom.
An electrically neutral particle (having no charge) that is also located inside the nucleus.

key_associations.extra_info: Discovered through the cathode ray tube experiment.
Goldstein discovered canal rays (positive rays), but Rutherford named the proton and proved its existence in the nucleus.
Discovered by bombarding beryllium with alpha particles.

important_facts.fact: Protons and neutrons are collectively referred to as 'nucleons' because they reside inside the nucleus.

sections.title: Historical Atomic Models
sections.description: Evolution of scientific theories and models proposed to explain the internal structure of an atom.

historical_events.significance: Proposed that matter is made of indivisible atoms, and all atoms of a given element are identical in mass and properties.
J.J. Thomson suggested the atom is a positively charged sphere with negatively charged electrons embedded within it.
Used gold foil to discover that an atom has a tiny, dense, positively charged core called the nucleus.
Niels Bohr postulated that electrons travel in specific circular orbits (discrete energy levels) around the nucleus without radiating energy.

sections.title: Atomic Number and Mass Number
sections.description: The fundamental identifiers of an element's atomic structure and chemical properties.

scientific_principles.application: Determines the chemical properties of an element. In a neutral atom, the number of protons equals the number of electrons (Z = p = e).
Represents the total mass of the atom, concentrated entirely in the nucleus. The number of neutrons can be calculated as n = A - Z.

sections.title: Isotopes, Isobars, and Isotones
sections.description: Classification of atoms based on similarities and differences in their subatomic particle counts.

key_concepts.explanation: Atoms of the same element having the same atomic number but different mass numbers (due to a different number of neutrons).
Atoms of different elements having the same mass number but different atomic numbers. Example: Argon (Ar-40) and Calcium (Ca-40).
Atoms of different elements that contain the exact same number of neutrons but a different number of protons.

important_facts.fact: Hydrogen is the only element whose isotopes have specific names: Protium (1H1), Deuterium (1H2), and Tritium (1H3).
Tritium (1H3) is the only naturally occurring radioactive isotope of hydrogen.

sections.title: Important Applications of Isotopes
sections.description: Radioactive isotopes have specialized uses in medical diagnostics, treatments, and various industries.

key_associations.extra_info: Used to determine the age of ancient organic materials and fossils in archaeology.
Emits high-energy gamma rays that destroy malignant tumor cells.

key_associations.associated_with: Treatment of Goiter and Thyroid disorders
key_associations.extra_info: Used as a tracer to evaluate thyroid gland function and treat hyperthyroidism.
Undergoes controlled nuclear fission to generate immense amounts of electrical energy.
Used as a medical tracer to study and monitor the human circulatory system.
